title: Long & short of SIR: What happens when exclusion is prioritised over inclusion
shows: Drèze's follow-up to his column with Yogendra Yadav. He sets the rolls of the major states against the Technical Group's projected adults for 2026 and finds them at 99 per cent before the revision and 85 per cent in the draft lists, and the twelve states with final lists at 97, 86 and 88 per cent. He argues that the rolls before the revision already missed many adults, perhaps up to 10 per cent on what he calls patchy evidence, and that dead, shifted and duplicate names hid the gap. Ground reports suggest most deletions of absent, shifted, dead and duplicate electors were legitimate, he writes, and the shortfall stayed because the second stage pursued documents from unmapped electors and added few through Form 6. Assam and Himachal Pradesh are left out of his table.
quote: For all major states together, pre-SIR lists add up to 99% of the corresponding adult population (see table).
In fact, ground reports from several states (including a careful state-wide survey in Rajasthan) suggest that majority of ASDD deletions are legitimate.
As a result, the pre-SIR lists were more or less in line with adult population counts, but this consistency was illusory: it masked the exclusion problem.
note: Read in full on 22 October 2026 (ET Commentary, last updated 21 October 2026, 11:21 pm IST). The table "Ratio of enrolled voters to adult population" cites the Technical Group on Population Projections, July 2020, and ECI press notes and press conferences, and excludes Assam and Himachal Pradesh. Recomputed from data/india/states.json for the 19 states with projected adults: 98.3 per cent before the revision and 84.4 per cent in the draft. For the 12 of them with final rolls (Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, West Bengal, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh, Kerala, Punjab, Odisha, Uttarakhand): 97.3, 85.7 and 87.5 per cent, or 88.4 per cent if West Bengal's 60,06,675 under adjudication are counted on the roll. All agree with the column's rounded figures. Shared on X as "less than 90% post-SIR", which sets the 99 per cent for all major states beside the 88 per cent for twelve of them.
